reasons.text: Buys feedstock inside a closed loop of 5 recyclers trading the same material (30% of its feedstock)
74% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity
Category III share of certificates is 59%, +57% versus what its process route can produce
61% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)
Electricity bought is only 0.40x the minimum needed for the tonnes claimed (119 kWh/t against at least 300)
Sold products equal only 21% of the output expected from the tonnes claimed

inspection_checklist: Trace the material flow between the plants in the loop (weighbridge slips, vehicle GPS); the same tonnes may be invoiced round a ring.
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
Cross-check the certificate generation dates and category mix against the plant's process route and stock registers.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Reconcile product sales with processed tonnes; contact the product buyers listed and verify that they received the material.
